slides.title: Module 2: Multilayer Perceptrons
points: From single perceptrons to trainable hidden layers: batch learning, online learning, backpropagation, XOR, optimization heuristics, and differentiation.
slides.takeaway: From single perceptrons to trainable hidden layers: batch learning, online learning, backpropagation, XOR, optimization heuristics, and differentiation.

slides.title: Module 2 has six syllabus checkpoints
Multilayer perceptrons add hidden layers between input and output
points: What changes from Module 1
A single perceptron can only draw a linear boundary. An MLP adds hidden neurons so the network can build intermediate representations before making an output decision.
Why it matters
Hidden layers allow nonlinear input-output mappings, making the MLP a foundation for later deep neural networks.
slides.takeaway: A single perceptron can only draw a linear boundary. An MLP adds hidden neurons so the network can build intermediate representations before making an output decision.

slides.title: An MLP is a directed, layered computation graph
points: Input layer
Hidden layer
Output layer
Signals flow forward; learning sends error information backward.
slides.takeaway: Signals flow forward; learning sends error information backward.

slides.title: Each layer applies the same neuron logic to new learned features
points: a(l-1) is the previous layer's activation vector.
W(l) and b(l) are the trainable weights and biases for layer l.
φ is applied to create the next layer's representation.
slides.takeaway: a(l-1) is the previous layer's activation vector.

slides.title: Batch learning views training as reducing total error
points: Etotal = Σp Ep
Each pattern p contributes an error term.
Weights are adjusted after the aggregate error or gradient is computed.
Batch updates are less noisy because they use the whole training set.
slides.takeaway: Each pattern p contributes an error term.

slides.title: Online learning updates immediately from each example
points: w ← w + Δwp
One pattern is presented, prediction is made, error is computed, and weights are changed.
The next example sees the newly updated network.
The update path can fluctuate, but learning can respond quickly.
slides.takeaway: One pattern is presented, prediction is made, error is computed, and weights are changed.

slides.title: Backpropagation is gradient descent made efficient for layered networks
points: Forward pass
Compute activations from input to output.
Loss
Measure the difference between output and target.
Backward pass
Propagate error signals from output to hidden layers.
extraPoints: Adjust weights in the direction that reduces error.
slides.takeaway: Compute activations from input to output.

slides.title: Backpropagation starts with a forward pass
points: Present an input vector to the input layer.
Compute weighted sums and activations layer by layer.
Produce the network output.
Store intermediate activations because the backward pass needs them.
slides.takeaway: Present an input vector to the input layer.
slides.formula: Present an input vector to the input layer.

slides.title: The output error tells the network what must change
points: e = d - y
d is the desired response for the training example.
y is the network output.
The error signal is converted into gradients for the output-layer weights.
slides.takeaway: d is the desired response for the training example.

slides.title: The backward pass assigns responsibility to earlier layers
points: δj = φ'(vj) Σk δk wkj
δ is the local gradient or error responsibility for a neuron.
Output-layer errors are pushed backward through connection weights.
The derivative of the activation controls how strongly a neuron can change.
slides.takeaway: δ is the local gradient or error responsibility for a neuron.

slides.title: Weight updates use local information at each connection
points: Δwji = η δj yi
η is the learning-rate parameter.
δj is the local gradient at the destination neuron.
yi is the activation arriving from the source neuron.
slides.takeaway: δj is the local gradient at the destination neuron.

slides.title: The XOR problem exposes why hidden layers are needed
points: No single straight line separates the 1s from the 0s.
Two hidden neurons can create two intermediate linear regions.
The output neuron combines those hidden regions to solve XOR.
slides.takeaway: No single straight line separates the 1s from the 0s.
slides.formula: No single straight line separates the 1s from the 0s.

slides.title: A hidden layer can turn XOR into a separable representation
points: Two hidden boundaries
One hidden neuron can detect one half-space.
Another hidden neuron can detect a second half-space.
The output layer combines hidden activations into the XOR answer.
slides.takeaway: One hidden neuron can detect one half-space.

slides.title: Learning rate is the first backpropagation heuristic to tune
points: Too small
Learning is stable but slow. The error decreases gradually and may require many epochs.
Too large
Updates can overshoot useful directions. Training may oscillate or diverge.
slides.takeaway: Learning is stable but slow. The error decreases gradually and may require many epochs.

slides.title: Momentum smooths noisy updates and helps cross shallow regions
points: Δw(t) = η δ y + α Δw(t-1)
η δ y is the current gradient-based correction.
α Δw(t-1) carries part of the previous correction forward.
Momentum can reduce zig-zag movement across narrow error surfaces.
slides.takeaway: η δ y is the current gradient-based correction.
slides.formula: Δw(t) = η δ y + α Δw(t-1)

slides.title: Initialization matters because symmetry blocks learning
points: If hidden neurons start with identical weights, they receive identical gradients.
Small random weights break symmetry between neurons.
Weights should not start so large that activations saturate.
Good initialization keeps signals and gradients in useful ranges.
slides.takeaway: If hidden neurons start with identical weights, they receive identical gradients.
slides.formula: Small random weights break symmetry between neurons.

slides.title: Activation saturation slows backpropagation
points: The issue
For sigmoid-like functions, very large positive or negative inputs create nearly flat output regions.
The effect
When φ'(v) is close to zero, local gradients become small and weight updates lose strength.
slides.takeaway: For sigmoid-like functions, very large positive or negative inputs create nearly flat output regions.

slides.title: Data scaling helps gradients behave consistently
points: Normalize or standardize input features before training.
Avoid one feature numerically dominating the weighted sum.
Scaled data often permits more reliable learning-rate choices.
Output encoding should match the activation and loss function.
slides.takeaway: Normalize or standardize input features before training.
slides.formula: Normalize or standardize input features before training.

slides.title: Stopping and validation prevent training from chasing noise
points: Training error
Backpropagation can continue reducing error on the training set as weights adapt.
Validation signal
A separate validation set helps decide when additional training no longer improves generalization.
slides.takeaway: Backpropagation can continue reducing error on the training set as weights adapt.

slides.title: Backpropagation is repeated application of the chain rule
points: The error depends on the output.
The output depends on the neuron's local field.
The local field depends on the weight being updated.
slides.takeaway: The output depends on the neuron's local field.

slides.title: Differentiation explains why smooth activations help
points: Perceptron threshold
A hard threshold is not useful for gradient-based learning because it is not smoothly differentiable.
MLP activations
Differentiable nonlinear activations allow gradients to flow backward through layers.
slides.takeaway: A hard threshold is not useful for gradient-based learning because it is not smoothly differentiable.

slides.title: The same chain-rule logic scales from one neuron to many layers
points: For an output neuron, compute the derivative of error with respect to its weights directly.
For a hidden neuron, multiply downstream error by the derivative of its activation.
Repeat this layer by layer until every weight has a gradient.
Update all trainable parameters using the chosen learning mode.
slides.takeaway: For an output neuron, compute the derivative of error with respect to its weights directly.
slides.formula: Repeat this layer by layer until every weight has a gradient.

slides.title: A good exam answer should connect algorithm, geometry, and calculus
points: MLP need
Hidden layers address nonlinear tasks such as XOR.
Learning mode
Batch and online learning differ by update timing.
Backprop steps
Forward pass, error, backward pass, update.
extraPoints: Local gradients come from the chain rule.
slides.takeaway: Hidden layers address nonlinear tasks such as XOR.
